name: Converly
author: Converly

sections.description:
Send server-side conversions to Google Ads, Meta Ads, Google Analytics 4, LinkedIn Ads, Microsoft Ads and more whenever a form is submitted on your site. Works with 100+ form builders, scheduling tools, chat widgets and more.

Converly is a conversion tracking plugin that sends conversions to Google Ads, Meta Ads (Facebook & Instagram), Microsoft Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Google Analytics 4 (GA4), TikTok, and more whenever someone converts on your website. It’s built for lead-generation businesses that need accurate conversion data to optimize their advertising campaigns.

When a visitor submits a form on your WordPress site, Converly captures the submission, enriches it with browser-side signals (click IDs, IP, user agent, device) and form data (email, name, phone), and sends conversion events directly to your ad platforms’ servers via their official APIs (such as the Google Ads Enhanced Conversions for Leads API, Meta Conversions API (CAPI), LinkedIn Conversions API, Microsoft Ads UET offline conversions, and GA4 Measurement Protocol).

You simply install the plugin, build your conversion flows in Converly’s drag-and-drop builder, and conversions start firing.

How It Works

  1. Install the plugin – Install Converly and create your Converly account to start your 14-day free trial.
  2. Build your conversion flow – In Converly’s Zapier-style drag-and-drop builder, pick a trigger (a form submission on your WordPress site) and your actions (send a conversion to Google Ads, Meta CAPI, GA4, etc.).
  3. See conversions in your ad platforms & analytics tools – Converly starts listening for form submissions and sending conversions to your ad platforms and analytics tools automatically.

What Problem Converly Solves

Browser-based conversion tracking (like using Google Tag Manager or tracking thank you page visits) is unreliable. Safari and iOS block third-party cookies, ad blockers prevent the Google Tag or Meta Pixel from loading on your site, and GTM containers get blocked easily. And when conversion data goes missing, your Smart Bidding, Advantage+ campaigns, and lookalike audiences optimize against incorrect data.

For ecommerce stores, server-side tracking has become standard. But for lead-generation businesses (such as agencies, B2B SaaS, service businesses, consultants, etc.), the tooling has lagged. Most “conversion tracking plugins” on WordPress focus on WooCommerce purchases. The few that handle form submissions either require Google Tag Manager to be set up server-side (expensive, technical) or only a couple of form tools.

Converly is built specifically for lead-gen businesses on WordPress. It supports every major form plugin out of the box, sends conversions server-side to every major ad platform, and requires no code, no tag manager, and no developer.

Why Use Converly

Simple to set up
Build your conversion flow in Converly’s drag-and-drop builder (similar to Zapier or HubSpot Workflows). Pick a trigger (a form being submitted) and select your actions (send a conversion to Google Ads, send a conversion to Meta, etc.). Works with WPForms, Gravity Forms, Contact Form 7, Ninja Forms, Forminator, Fluent Forms, Formidable Forms and more out of the box.

Sends conversions server-side for better reliability
Converly sends conversions directly to each ad platform’s API. This bypasses ad blockers, Safari ITP, iOS 14+ restrictions, and other browser-level tracking prevention to give you more accurate conversion tracking. In fact, Google’s own data shows server-side tracking increases tracked conversions by 19% (Meta’s data shows a 23% increase).

Sends more data for improved match rate
Converly captures browser signals (Google Click ID, Facebook Click ID, Microsoft Click ID, IP address, user agent, device) AND form data (name, email, phone, company) and sends it all with each conversion. According to Meta’s own data, this results in a 95%+ match rate (versus a 40% match rate from browser-only data).

Full debug log
Conversion tracking can often be a black box, and you have no idea whether it’s working properly or not. Converly gives you a full log of every conversion, showing exactly what data was captured, what data was sent to each ad platform, whether it was received successfully, etc. This gives you confidence that your conversion tracking is working properly and allows you to spot issues when it isn’t.

Proper support from analytics experts
Ever tried to ask Google or Meta to help with your conversion tracking setup? You probably got nowhere. Our team has 20+ years experience in marketing analytics and is on hand to help make sure your conversion tracking is set up properly.

Supported Form Builders, Scheduling Tools, Chatbots, etc.

Converly works with every major form plugin, page builder, popup tool, LMS, membership plugin, and embedded SaaS form on WordPress, with no configuration required.

WordPress form plugins

Track form submissions as conversions in your ad platforms and analytics tools. Converly works with the following WordPress form plugins:

  • Gravity Forms
  • WPForms
  • Contact Form 7
  • Ninja Forms
  • Fluent Forms
  • Formidable Forms
  • Forminator
  • WS Form
  • Everest Forms
  • HappyForms
  • SureForms

Page builder forms

Track submissions from forms built with your page builder as conversions in your ad platforms and analytics tools. Converly works with the following page builders:

  • Elementor forms
  • Divi forms
  • Bricks forms
  • Beaver Builder forms
  • Brizy forms
  • Avada forms
  • SeedProd forms

Embedded scheduling tools

Track meeting bookings as conversions in your ad platforms and analytics tools. Converly works with the following scheduling tools:

  • Calendly
  • Cal.com
  • Acuity Scheduling
  • YouCanBookMe
  • Chili Piper
  • OnceHub
  • HubSpot Meetings
  • Square Appointments
  • Mindbody

Embedded SaaS form tools

Track submissions from embedded SaaS forms, marketing tools, and CRMs as conversions in your ad platforms and analytics tools. Converly works with the following embedded form tools:

  • Mailchimp
  • HubSpot Forms
  • Typeform
  • Jotform
  • Klaviyo
  • ActiveCampaign
  • Salesforce Web-to-Lead
  • Constant Contact
  • Brevo
  • Zoho Forms
  • Marketo
  • Pardot
  • GetResponse
  • AWeber
  • MailerLite
  • Kit (formerly ConvertKit)
  • Keap
  • Formstack
  • Tally
  • Fillout
  • Paperform
  • HighLevel (GoHighLevel)
  • Pipedrive
  • FormAssembly
  • Formsite
  • GetLeadForms

Popups, optins, and lead capture plugins

Track optins and lead captures from your popup tools as conversions in your ad platforms and analytics tools. Converly works with the following popup and lead capture plugins:

  • OptinMonster
  • Popup Maker
  • Popup Builder
  • Hello Bar
  • Bloom

WordPress LMS plugins

Track course enrollments as conversions in your ad platforms and analytics tools. Converly works with the following WordPress LMS plugins:

  • LearnDash
  • LearnPress
  • Sensei LMS
  • Tutor LMS

WordPress membership plugins

Track new member signups as conversions in your ad platforms and analytics tools. Converly works with the following membership plugins:

  • Paid Memberships Pro
  • ProfilePress
  • Ultimate Member
  • WishList Member

WordPress email newsletter plugins

Track newsletter signups as conversions in your ad platforms and analytics tools. Converly works with the following email newsletter plugins:

  • MailPoet
  • Newsletter

Embedded chat widgets

Track new chat conversations and lead captures as conversions in your ad platforms and analytics tools. Converly works with the following chat widgets:

  • Intercom
  • LiveChat
  • Drift
  • Tawk.to
  • HubSpot Chat
  • Zoho SalesIQ
  • Qualified

Field service & appointment platforms

Track booked jobs as conversions in your ad platforms and analytics tools, for HVAC, plumbing, electrical, lawn care, and other home-service businesses running Google Ads. Get true cost-per-job reporting in your ad accounts. Converly works with the following field service platforms:

  • Jobber
  • ServiceTitan
  • Housecall Pro

Supported Ad Platforms & Analytics Tools

Ad Platforms

Send conversions server-side to all the major ad platforms via their official conversion APIs. Converly works with the following ad platforms:

  • Google Ads via the Google Ads Enhanced Conversions for Leads API
  • Meta (Facebook & Instagram) via the Meta Conversions API (CAPI)
  • Microsoft Ads via Microsoft Ads UET offline conversions
  • LinkedIn Ads via the LinkedIn Conversions API
  • TikTok Ads via the TikTok Events API
  • Snapchat Ads via the Snapchat Conversions API
  • X Ads (formerly Twitter) via the X Conversions API
  • Reddit Ads via the Reddit Conversions API
  • AdRoll, Taboola, and BuySellAds

Analytics Tools

Send events server-side to your analytics and reporting tools. Converly works with the following analytics tools:

  • Google Analytics 4 (GA4) via the GA4 Measurement Protocol
  • Plausible Analytics, Fathom Analytics, Simple Analytics, Pirsch Analytics, and GoSquared for privacy-friendly analytics

For the full list of 100+ integrations, see converly.io/integrations.

Who Converly Is For

  • Lead-generation businesses running paid ads on Google, Meta, LinkedIn, or Microsoft and losing conversion data to browser restrictions
  • Marketing agencies managing conversion tracking across multiple client sites who want a reliable, scalable solution that works with all the tools their clients use
  • B2B SaaS companies running LinkedIn Ads and Google Ads for trial signups and demo bookings
  • Service businesses (legal, financial, professional services, coaches, consultants) running Google Ads, Meta Ads, etc. for lead generation
  • Home-service businesses (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, lawn care, cleaning) running Google Ads, Meta Ads, etc. and using Jobber, ServiceTitan, or Housecall Pro to book new jobs
  • Course creators and educators running Meta and Google Ads to drive enrollments on LearnDash, LearnPress, Tutor LMS, Sensei, or embedded platforms like Kajabi, Teachable, and Thinkific
  • Membership site owners running ads to drive new signups via Paid Memberships Pro, ProfilePress, Ultimate Member, or WishList Member
  • Anyone whose Google Ads or Meta campaigns are optimizing against incomplete conversion data

Consent Mode & Privacy

Converly supports Google Consent Mode v2 and Microsoft Consent Mode, sending or blocking conversions based on your existing Consent Management Platform (CMP). Compatible with CookieYes, Complianz, Real Cookie Banner, Cookiebot, and Iubenda.

All personally identifiable information (PII), such as email, phone, and name, is hashed using SHA-256 before being sent to ad platforms, in line with each platform’s CAPI requirements.

Pricing

The Converly WordPress plugin is free to install, and connecting it requires a Converly account.

Every Converly account comes with a 14-day free trial, so you can install the plugin, build your conversion flows, and confirm everything is working before you pay. After the trial, paid plans start at $19 per month. See converly.io/pricing for full details.

Why Trust Converly

Converly is built by the team behind Attributer, a marketing attribution tool trusted by 1,100+ businesses to capture UTM and click-ID data from their lead forms. Converly extends the same philosophy of simple, reliable marketing data infrastructure for lead-gen businesses to server-side conversion tracking.

External Services

Converly is a third-party service (a separate SaaS operated by Converly). This plugin is a free client to that service and requires it to function, because the attribution and conversion tracking happen on Converly’s servers. Below is exactly what is sent, when, and to where.

When you connect your site (clicking Sign Up or Log In). The plugin sends your site address (home URL), your site title, and a randomly generated per-site identifier to Converly, and completes a secure sign-in (OAuth) exchange. Converly returns an access credential that is stored on your server only.

The tracking script (after you connect and while tracking is on). Your public pages load Converly’s tracking script from Converly’s content delivery network (js.converly.io). As part of the Converly service, that script then fetches additional code and configuration from Converly, sets first-party cookies in the visitor’s browser, and keeps a short retry queue in the browser’s local storage for events that fail to send.

Form submissions (when a visitor submits a form). Converly’s script reads the submitted form fields, which can include personal data such as name, email and phone, together with the page URL, the referring URL, and marketing parameters such as UTM tags and ad click identifiers, and sends them to Converly for conversion tracking.

Managing your account (while you use the plugin). When you view flows, subscription status, or make changes, your site’s server calls the Converly API on your behalf using the stored credential.

Data is sent to Converly at https://app.converly.io (the API), and the tracking script is served from https://js.converly.io. By using this plugin you agree to Converly’s Terms of Service (https://converly.io/terms) and Privacy Policy (https://converly.io/privacy-policy). As the site owner, you are responsible for obtaining any visitor consent required by law (for example, under the GDPR) before this tracking runs. The plugin provides an on/off setting for tracking and a developer filter (converly_should_enqueue_loader) so consent-management plugins can control when the tracking script loads.

Privacy

On your WordPress server the plugin stores: the Converly access credential, your Converly account and site identifiers, the connected administrator’s email address, the plugin’s settings, and short-lived sign-in handshake data. Visitor data captured at form submission is processed by the Converly script in the visitor’s browser and sent to Converly; it is not stored in your WordPress database.

When you delete the plugin, this local data is removed and the plugin attempts to disconnect your site from Converly. The plugin also registers suggested privacy-policy text (Settings → Privacy → Policy Guide) describing the Converly service for you to adapt.

See converly.io/privacy-policy for our full privacy policy.

Support

Need help with setup or troubleshooting? The Converly team is available via:

  • Email: help@converly.io
  • Help docs: help.converly.io
  • In-app live chat (available to all account holders)

Most tickets are answered within a few hours during business hours.
sections.installation:
1. From your WordPress admin, go to Plugins → Add New and search for “Converly”.
  2. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  3. Go to Converly in your WordPress admin sidebar and click Sign Up (or Log In if you already have a Converly account).
  4. From the Converly menu, create your first conversion flow. This opens Converly’s drag-and-drop builder in your Converly account, where you pick a form, choose the ad platforms to send conversions to, and publish.
  5. That’s it. Conversions will start firing the next time someone submits a form on your site.

For step-by-step setup guides, see help.converly.io/wordpress.
sections.faq:
Does Converly work with WPForms?

Yes. Converly auto-detects WPForms submissions (both Lite and Pro) with no configuration required. Just install Converly, connect your ad accounts, and select WPForms as your trigger.

Does Converly work with Gravity Forms?

Yes. Gravity Forms is fully supported out of the box. Converly captures the submission, all form field data, and any hidden fields (UTMs, click IDs, etc.) and sends it server-side to your ad platforms.

Does Converly work with Contact Form 7, Ninja Forms, Forminator, Fluent Forms, and Formidable Forms?

Yes. All major WordPress form plugins are supported with zero configuration.

Does Converly work with Elementor Forms?

Yes. Elementor’s built-in form widget is supported automatically. Divi, Bricks, Beaver Builder, Brizy, Avada, and SeedProd forms are also supported.

Does Converly work with embedded HubSpot, Typeform, Jotform, Calendly, or Cal.com forms?

Yes. Converly detects embedded forms and scheduling widgets from these tools on your WordPress site and tracks submissions and bookings as conversions.

Can I track Calendly or Cal.com bookings as conversions?

Yes. Converly fires a conversion event when a visitor completes a booking via embedded Calendly, Cal.com, Acuity Scheduling, HubSpot Meetings, OnceHub, YouCanBookMe, Chili Piper, or Square Appointments widgets, so you can attribute meeting bookings back to your Google Ads, Meta, and LinkedIn campaigns.

Can I track LearnDash, LearnPress, Tutor LMS, or Sensei course enrollments as conversions?

Yes. Converly tracks course enrollments from all major WordPress LMS plugins as conversion events, perfect for course creators running Meta and Google Ads to drive enrollments.

Can I track membership signups as conversions?

Yes. Converly supports Paid Memberships Pro, ProfilePress, Ultimate Member, and WishList Member. New member signups fire as conversions to your ad platforms.

Does Converly work for home service businesses using Jobber, ServiceTitan, or Housecall Pro?

Yes. This is one of Converly’s strongest use cases. Most HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and home-service businesses can’t measure the real ROI of their Google Ads because conversion tracking stops at the lead form. Converly tracks booked jobs from Jobber, ServiceTitan, and Housecall Pro as conversions in Google Ads, so Smart Bidding optimizes against real jobs booked rather than just form fills.

Can I track chat conversations from Intercom, Drift, LiveChat, or HubSpot Chat as conversions?

Yes. Converly tracks new chat conversations and qualified leads from all major chat tools as conversion events.

Does Converly work with Mailchimp, Klaviyo, ActiveCampaign, or other marketing automation forms?

Yes. Embedded forms from Mailchimp, Klaviyo, ActiveCampaign, Brevo, Constant Contact, AWeber, GetResponse, MailerLite, Kit (ConvertKit), Keap, HighLevel, Marketo, Pardot, and Salesforce Web-to-Lead are all auto-detected.

Does Converly support webinar registrations from Demio, Livestorm, or WebinarJam?

Yes. Webinar registrations fire as conversion events, so you can attribute them back to the ad campaigns that drove them.

What is server-side conversion tracking, and why does it matter?

Server-side tracking sends conversion data directly from your server to each ad platform’s API, bypassing the browser entirely. This avoids data loss from ad blockers, Safari Intelligent Tracking Prevention (ITP), iOS 14+ restrictions, and browser cookie limits. Google’s own data shows server-side tracking recovers ~19% more conversions; Meta reports a 23% increase.

How is Converly different from PixelYourSite, Pixel Manager, or ConversionBridge?

Most existing conversion tracking plugins are built for WooCommerce ecommerce stores, tracking add-to-cart, checkout, and purchase events. Converly is built specifically for lead-generation businesses tracking form submissions across multiple ad platforms. It also offers true server-side conversion tracking via each platform’s official API, rather than just pixel-based tracking.

How is Converly different from setting up server-side Google Tag Manager?

Server-side GTM is powerful but requires significant technical setup: provisioning a tagging server, configuring tags and triggers, managing dataLayer events, and ongoing maintenance. Converly does the same job of sending conversions server-side via each platform’s official API, with no GTM server, no dataLayer engineering, and no developer required.

Does Converly support Google Ads Enhanced Conversions for Leads?

Yes. Converly hashes the visitor’s email, phone, and name from the form submission and sends it via the Google Ads API as enhanced conversion data. This dramatically improves match rates with Google’s logged-in users and lets Google Smart Bidding optimize against real conversion outcomes.

Does Converly support Meta CAPI (Conversions API)?

Yes. Meta CAPI is fully supported. Converly sends events directly to Meta’s servers via the Conversions API, hashes all PII per Meta’s requirements, deduplicates against any client-side pixel events, and includes the Facebook Click ID (FBCLID) for high Event Match Quality.

Does Converly support LinkedIn Conversions API?

Yes. LinkedIn CAPI is supported, with PII hashing and LinkedIn Click ID (LICLID) handling for B2B lead conversions.

Does Converly support Microsoft Ads conversion tracking?

Yes. Converly sends offline conversions to Microsoft Ads via the UET API, including the Microsoft Click ID (MSCLKID) for accurate attribution to Bing search and Microsoft Audience Network campaigns.

Does Converly support GA4 server-side tracking?

Yes. Converly sends form submission events to GA4 via the Measurement Protocol, alongside any client-side gtag events you already have running.

Will Converly slow down my site?

No. The Converly plugin is lightweight. It adds Converly’s tracking script, which loads asynchronously, and all conversion processing happens on Converly’s servers rather than on your site. There’s no impact on page load times or Core Web Vitals.

Is Converly compatible with WordPress caching plugins?

Yes. Converly works with WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, LiteSpeed Cache, and other caching plugins. Because conversion data is sent server-side, page-level caching doesn’t affect tracking.

Is Converly compatible with Consent Mode v2?

Yes. Converly supports Google Consent Mode v2 and Microsoft Consent Mode, and works with major CMPs including CookieYes, Complianz, Real Cookie Banner, Cookiebot, and Iubenda.

Is my form submission data secure?

Yes. All data in transit is encrypted via TLS. PII fields (email, phone, name) are hashed using SHA-256 before being sent to ad platforms, in line with each platform’s CAPI requirements. Converly does not store form submission data longer than needed to send conversions; you can configure 0-day retention in your account settings.

Does Converly require a paid account?

The Converly WordPress plugin is free to install, but it connects to your Converly account to send conversions. Every account starts with a 14-day free trial, so you can get everything set up and working before you pay. After the trial, paid plans start at $19 per month. See converly.io/pricing for details.

What happens if a conversion fails to send?

Converly automatically retries failed conversion sends with exponential backoff. If a conversion ultimately can’t be delivered (e.g. because an ad account has been disconnected), you’ll see it in the event log with an error message so you can fix the issue and replay if needed.

Can I see exactly what data was sent to each ad platform?

Yes. Every conversion appears in the Converly event log with the full payload sent, the response received from each ad platform, and any error messages. This is one of Converly’s core features: no more black-box conversion tracking.

Where can I get help?

Email help@converly.io, browse the docs at help.converly.io, or use the in-app live chat. Most queries are answered within a few hours during business hours.

Does Converly work with multisite WordPress installs?

Yes, using per-site activation. Activate Converly on each individual site in your network (rather than network-activating it) and connect each site to your Converly account. Network-wide activation is not supported in this version.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • Initial release of Converly for WordPress.
  • Server-side conversion tracking to Google Ads, Meta Ads, Microsoft Ads, LinkedIn Ads, GA4, TikTok, and more.
  • Drag-and-drop conversion flow builder.
  • Auto-detection of all major WordPress form plugins, page builders, and embedded SaaS forms.
  • Full conversion event log.
  • Google Consent Mode v2 and Microsoft Consent Mode support.

External Services

Converly is a third-party service (a separate SaaS operated by Converly). This plugin is a free client to that service and requires it to function, because the attribution and conversion tracking happen on Converly’s servers. Below is exactly what is sent, when, and to where.

When you connect your site (clicking Sign Up or Log In). The plugin sends your site address (home URL), your site title, and a randomly generated per-site identifier to Converly, and completes a secure sign-in (OAuth) exchange. Converly returns an access credential that is stored on your server only.

The tracking script (after you connect and while tracking is on). Your public pages load Converly’s tracking script from Converly’s content delivery network (js.converly.io). As part of the Converly service, that script then fetches additional code and configuration from Converly, sets first-party cookies in the visitor’s browser, and keeps a short retry queue in the browser’s local storage for events that fail to send.

Form submissions (when a visitor submits a form). Converly’s script reads the submitted form fields, which can include personal data such as name, email and phone, together with the page URL, the referring URL, and marketing parameters such as UTM tags and ad click identifiers, and sends them to Converly for conversion tracking.

Managing your account (while you use the plugin). When you view flows, subscription status, or make changes, your site’s server calls the Converly API on your behalf using the stored credential.

Data is sent to Converly at https://app.converly.io (the API), and the tracking script is served from https://js.converly.io. By using this plugin you agree to Converly’s Terms of Service (https://converly.io/terms) and Privacy Policy (https://converly.io/privacy-policy). As the site owner, you are responsible for obtaining any visitor consent required by law (for example, under the GDPR) before this tracking runs. The plugin provides an on/off setting for tracking and a developer filter (converly_should_enqueue_loader) so consent-management plugins can control when the tracking script loads.

Privacy

On your WordPress server the plugin stores: the Converly access credential, your Converly account and site identifiers, the connected administrator’s email address, the plugin’s settings, and short-lived sign-in handshake data. Visitor data captured at form submission is processed by the Converly script in the visitor’s browser and sent to Converly; it is not stored in your WordPress database.

When you delete the plugin, this local data is removed and the plugin attempts to disconnect your site from Converly. The plugin also registers suggested privacy-policy text (Settings → Privacy → Policy Guide) describing the Converly service for you to adapt.

See converly.io/privacy-policy for our full privacy policy.
